_about: Reference evidence registers, written to test the rule check and the safeguards without a model. They are not used to score the agent: the agent is scored against cases/expected_outcomes.csv. Each entry has the arguments of the record_evidence tool.

C01.quote: drew the area as suspected because it lies below the former front line on the ridge
C01.note: An early survey record drawn from wartime maps and interviews, with no item, accident or marking; its reliability has not been assessed.

C01.quote: shows one minefield, laid on the eastern ridge
C01.note: A minefield record shown to be reliable on a completed clearance task places the unit's minefield outside the area.

C01.quote: The minefield on the eastern ridge was cleared in 2009
C01.note: The completion report and handover certificate document the clearance of that minefield, outside the area.

C01.quote: I have mown the lower meadow every summer since 2008
C01.note: First-hand safe use of both meadows by the landowner for 16 to 18 years; he also placed the cow incident on the eastern ridge.

C01.quote: gather herbs and mushrooms on both meadows every spring and autumn
C01.note: First-hand use of both meadows by women, consulted separately.

C01.quote: We laid mines only on the eastern ridge
C01.note: A first-hand source who served on the ridge says that no mines were laid on the meadows, and places the cow incident on the eastern ridge.

C01.quote: he had heard that a cow was hurt
C01.note: A second-hand report with no place; two first-hand sources place the incident on the eastern ridge, outside the area.

C01.quote: saw no mines, fragments, signs, fencing or craters
C01.note: The team's own walk of the paths, the edges and the track found no physical evidence.

C02.quote: lists a dangerous area near the former army position
C02.note: An approximate record with no boundary, items or accidents; its reliability has not been assessed.

C02.quote: the 2010 dangerous area is this same minefield
C02.note: A documented desk review shows that the 2010 record duplicates the army minefield beside the position.

C02.quote: The minefield beside the position was cleared in 2014
C02.note: The completion report and handover certificate document the clearance of that minefield.

C02.quote: We came back in 2017 and have grown vegetables here every year
C02.note: First-hand daily use since 2017 and 2018, including digging wells and putting up fences.

C02.quote: have found nothing in eight years
C02.note: First-hand use by women, consulted separately.

C02.quote: no accident and no item has been reported in the village since resettlement began
C02.note: The village officer's records hold no accident and no item since resettlement.

C02.quote: saw no items, signs or fencing
C02.note: The team's walk found no physical evidence, and the minefield site has the marker stones of a cleared site.

C03.quote: recorded the area as suspected because it lies near former positions on the border and people avoided it
C03.note: A baseline record based on nearby positions and avoidance, with no mines or accidents in the area.

C03.quote: ploughed these fields with a tractor every year since 2016
C03.note: First-hand ploughing of part A by tractor for ten years.

C03.quote: We plant and harvest there every season
C03.note: First-hand use of part A by a woman farmer.

C03.quote: was told years ago that a buffalo was killed by a mine
C03.note: A second-hand report of an accident whose place is not known: indirect evidence for the strip.

C03.quote: because people say it is dangerous
C03.note: Avoidance out of fear, with no find or accident named, is not evidence on its own.

C03.quote: saw no items, signs or fencing
C03.note: The team walked part A and the edge of the strip but did not enter the strip, so this counts for part A only.

C03.quote: has recorded no accident in these fields since he took office in 2015
C03.note: No accident recorded since 2015; it does not explain the buffalo report, whose date is not known.

C04.quote: Three EOD spot tasks in 2021–2024 recorded submunitions destroyed in the valley-floor plots
C04.note: Confirmed EOD spot tasks at known plots: evidence points for cluster munition remnant survey.

C04.quote: farmers marked six places in the valley-floor plots and two on the slopes
C04.note: First-hand finders at places marked on the community map.

C04.quote: Bombing data in the national database show strikes in the valley
C04.note: Bombing data help to plan survey but are not direct evidence of cluster munition remnants.

C04.quote: a scrap dealer's yard in the village, where people brought items they had collected
C04.note: Items brought from elsewhere to a scrap yard are not evidence about the plots.

C04.quote: Nobody has been hurt in the plots since 2015
C04.note: No accidents since 2015, but finds continue, so it explains none of the direct evidence.

C04.quote: No mines are reported in the village or the valley
C04.note: No mines are known, which matters because cluster munition remnant survey cannot be used where there is a landmine threat.

C04.quote: saw no items on the surface
C04.note: Nothing was seen on the surface, with most plots under crops, so it explains none of the reported finds.

C05.quote: lists the area as suspected because troops were present in the village in 2022
C05.note: A settlement-level record; the past presence of troops is indirect evidence under the criteria box.

C05.quote: These fields must be mined; the soldiers were everywhere around the village
C05.note: A second-hand claim from someone who was not in the village during the occupation.

C05.quote: I harvested wheat on the open fields in 2025 with my own machinery
C05.note: First-hand use of part A, but for one season only.

C05.quote: shows old fighting positions and trenches along the forest belt, and several craters
C05.note: Positions, trenches and craters seen by the team in imagery; craters without items are indirect evidence under the criteria box.

C05.quote: soldiers dug in along the forest belt but did not go onto the open fields
C05.note: First-hand sources who stayed during the occupation outweigh the administrator's second-hand claim for part A; for the forest belt the same account is indirect evidence, as E4 already shows.

C05.quote: The team walked the field tracks and saw no items, signs or fencing
C05.note: The team walked the field tracks; it did not enter the forest belt.

C06.quote: the boundary of sector 4 includes the margin under review
C06.note: The margin lies inside a CHA drawn as a wide band; the record holds no direct evidence in the margin itself.

C06.quote: all mines were found in a narrow belt along the line of the old fence
C06.note: Completion reports in the neighbouring sectors found mines only in a narrow belt along the old fence.

C06.quote: the margin lies beyond the belt in which mines were found in the neighbouring sectors
C06.note: A desk assessment against reliable clearance records.

C06.quote: I have grown maize on this land every year since 2012
C06.note: First-hand ploughing of the margin for 14 years.

C06.quote: they collect firewood along the margin and walk through it to the river
C06.note: First-hand use of the margin by women, consulted separately.

C06.quote: no items, signs or posts in the margin itself
C06.note: The team saw fence posts on the minefield line, well away from the margin, and nothing in the margin.

C07.quote: described a minefield they helped to lay across the road approach and along the riverbank
C07.note: First-hand accounts of laying from former combatants, which IMAS 08.10 lists as indirect evidence; the physical evidence below confirms them.

C07.quote: the remains of an old fence and two rusted warning signs along the riverbank
C07.note: Fencing and warning signs associated with contamination, seen by the team.

C07.quote: A goat was killed by an explosion on the road approach in 2023
C07.note: An animal accident at a known spot, seen by the herder.

C07.quote: heard and saw an explosion on the riverbank upstream of the crossing
C07.note: A detonation during a bush fire, seen by first-hand witnesses.

C07.quote: People cross the river further upstream on a footpath and do not use the road approach
C07.note: Land and road left unused because of the danger.

C07.quote: plans to upgrade the road and rebuild the crossing in 2027
C07.note: Planned road works raise the priority but are not evidence of explosive ordnance.

C08.quote: removed two improvised devices from the front of the berm in 2019
C08.note: A located removal of devices, in a police record checked with the station.

C08.quote: A herder was injured by an explosion in front of the southern half of the berm in 2021
C08.note: An accident at a known spot, documented in police and hospital records.

C08.quote: a line of disturbed ground in front of it along its whole length
C08.note: Disturbed ground in imagery suggests, but does not confirm, devices along the whole berm.

C08.quote: Families have not used the land in front of the berm since they returned in 2018
the berm was the front of the occupiers' defences around the village
C08.note: A first-hand account of the berm's military use.

C08.quote: a red-painted warning that villagers made near the southern end of the berm
C08.note: A local warning associated with contamination, seen by the team.

C09.quote: described mines laid on the upper terraces and on either side of the path
C09.note: A first-hand account from the commander who ordered the laying.

C09.quote: marked the edge of the upper terraces and both sides of the path with lines of red-painted stones
C09.note: Local marking associated with contamination, seen by the team.

C09.quote: Two cows were killed by explosions on the third upper terrace
C09.note: Animal accidents at known spots, seen by the owners.

C09.quote: A shepherd was injured by an explosion on the path in 2016
C09.note: An accident at a known spot, from a witness who was with the victim.

C09.quote: some men removed mines from the path themselves in the early 2000s
C09.note: Informal removal by people without accreditation is not clearance; it suggests mines on the path, at second hand.

C09.quote: The upper terraces have not been farmed since the 1990s
C09.note: Good land left unfarmed since the 1990s.

C10.quote: its source and the date it was entered are unknown, and it gives no items or accidents
C10.note: A record of unknown source, whose reliability cannot be assessed.

C10.quote: people do not go there because of the war
C10.note: A phone report from someone who saw nothing himself; the source of what people say is unknown.

C10.quote: the team's desk assessment found no record of fighting there
C10.note: No record of fighting, from records of unassessed reliability; not enough to explain the database record.

C11.quote: holds a record of a minefield of anti-vehicle and anti-personnel mines upstream of the crossing
C11.note: A migrated record of a minefield upstream, outside the area, with an uncertain position and unassessed reliability; the likely source of items carried downstream.

C11.quote: found and destroyed one anti-vehicle mine on the wadi bank below the crossing
C11.note: A confirmed find in part B; the mine was carried by a flood, so it is evidence of the flood path, which the criteria box says calls for survey of the path it travelled.

C11.quote: Our families have camped on the terrace by the water point in every year with rain since 2008
C11.note: First-hand safe use of the terrace for 18 years.

C11.quote: his family also camps and grazes its animals on the terrace in years with rain
C11.note: A second first-hand source of safe use of the terrace.

C11.quote: holds one livestock incident near the wadi crossing
C11.note: An accident whose place cannot be determined accurately: indirect evidence.

C11.quote: saw no explosive ordnance on its surface; the check covered only the surface of the track
C11.note: A surface check of the track only; it does not explain the flood-carried mine.

C11.quote: the main flood channel has moved since the 1980s
C11.note: Shifting flood deposits suggest that items may have been carried across the wadi bed; the terrace lies above the flood line.

C11.quote: no strike sites or explosive incidents have been recorded near the crossing
C11.note: Weak evidence of absence: neither party has shared where it fought.

C11.quote: the team could not go near it under restricted-area instructions
C11.note: Part C was never reached; there is no evidence either way, so it can be neither cancelled nor targeted.
